newsitem.title: UK: LME copper crumbles below $2,300 in late trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper crumbles below $2,300 in late trade.

text.p: Copper prices fell sharply by some $80 per tonne in late trading on Tuesday amid fund selling and long liquidation, dealers and analysts said.
By 1800 GMT three months copper was quoted at $2,290/2,294 per tonne, compared to $2,368 at the London Metal Exchange (LME) kerb close.
"Everyone's trying to bale out of it at moment. There's quite a lot of volume even though the market's quite thin," a trader said.
Analysts said copper hit sell stops below the $2,355 support area and again under $2,325.
"There has been long liquidation as well as fund selling out of the U.S.," said analyst William Adams of brokers Rudolf Wolff.
Below current levels, the $2,250 area -- last seen in mid-April -- will be an important chart point for copper, he added.
Meanwhile cash to threes backwardation held basically steady at $130/$135, just $10 narrower than at the close.
Traders said the backwardation was the only factor in the market that had been supporting prices.
But rising stocks and the expectation of more inventory rises in coming weeks has been pressuring the market, they said.
The other metals were weaker with copper. Aluminium was last quoted at $1,555/57, versus $1,565 at the close while nickel was at $6,840/6,850, from $6,935.
